ayahs.1: These opening letters—known as the muqatta'at—are among the signs whose full meaning Allah kept with Himself. They open the surah by reminding the reader that this Book is from beyond human authorship: approach it with humility, not arrogance.
ayahs.2: This is a reminder of your Rabb's mercy to His servant Zachariah—
ayahs.3: when he called upon his Rabb in private,
ayahs.4: saying: "My Rabb, my bones have grown frail and grey hair spreads across my head, yet I have never been disappointed calling upon You, my Rabb.
ayahs.5: I fear for my people after me. My wife is barren—so grant me, by Your grace, an heir
ayahs.6: who will inherit prophethood from me and from the family of Jacob, and make him, my Rabb, pleasing to You."
ayahs.7: The angels announced: "O Zachariah, We give you good news of a son whose name will be John—a name We have given to no one before."
ayahs.8: He wondered: "My Rabb, how can I have a son when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age?"
ayahs.9: The angel replied: "So it will be. Your Rabb says: It is easy for Me—as I created you before when you were nothing."
ayahs.10: Zachariah said: "My Rabb, grant me a sign." He replied: "Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three nights, though you are healthy."
ayahs.11: He came out to his people from the sanctuary, signalling them to glorify Allah morning and evening.
ayahs.12: O John, hold firmly to the Scripture. We granted him wisdom while still a child,
ayahs.13: and purity and compassion from Us. He was one of taqwa—living with Allah-consciousness.
ayahs.14: Kind to his parents, neither arrogant nor disobedient.
ayahs.15: Peace upon him the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive.
ayahs.16: And mention in the Book Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place in the east,
ayahs.17: screening herself from them. We sent Our angel Gabriel, appearing before her as a perfectly formed man.
ayahs.18: She said: "I seek refuge in the Rahman—whose mercy encompasses all creation—from you. Leave me if you have taqwa."
ayahs.19: He said: "I am only a messenger from your Rabb, sent to bless you with a pure son."
ayahs.20: She wondered: "How can I have a son when no man has touched me, nor am I unchaste?"
ayahs.21: He replied: "So it will be. Your Rabb says: It is easy for Me. We will make him a sign for humanity and a mercy from Us. It is already decreed."
ayahs.22: She conceived him and withdrew with him to a remote place.
ayahs.23: Labour pains drove her to a palm tree. She cried: "I wish I had died before this and been forgotten long ago."
ayahs.24: A voice reassured her from below: "Do not grieve. Your Rabb has provided a stream at your feet.
ayahs.25: Shake the trunk of this palm toward you—it will drop fresh ripe dates upon you.
ayahs.26: Eat, drink, and let your heart be at ease. If you see anyone, say: I have vowed silence to the Rahman, so I am not speaking to anyone today."
ayahs.27: She returned to her people carrying him. They said in shock: "O Mary, you have done something terrible!
ayahs.28: O sister of Aaron, your father was not indecent, nor was your mother unchaste."
ayahs.29: She pointed to the baby. They said: "How can we speak to an infant in the cradle?"
ayahs.30: Jesus declared: "I am truly a servant of Allah. He has destined me to receive the Scripture and be a prophet.
ayahs.31: He made me a blessing wherever I go, and enjoined salah and zakat upon me as long as I live,
ayahs.32: and to be kind to my mother. He did not make me arrogant or defiant.
ayahs.33: Peace upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive."
ayahs.34: That is Jesus, son of Mary—a word of truth about which they dispute.
ayahs.35: It is not for Allah to take a son. Glory be to Him. When He decrees a matter, He only says "Be," and it is.
ayahs.36: Jesus also declared: "Allah is my Rabb and your Rabb, so worship Him alone. This is the Straight Path—the way of living that pleases Allah."
ayahs.37: Yet their factions differed about him. Woe to those who reject the truth when they face a tremendous Day.
ayahs.38: How clearly they will hear and see the Day they come to Us. But today the wrongdoers are clearly astray.
ayahs.39: Warn them of the Day of Regret, when every matter is settled while they remain heedless, refusing iman.
ayahs.40: It is We who will inherit the earth and all upon it. To Us they will all return.
ayahs.41: And mention Abraham in the Book. He was a man of truth and a prophet.
ayahs.42: When he said to his father: "O dear father, why do you worship what cannot hear or see, nor benefit you at all?
ayahs.43: O dear father, I have received knowledge you have not received—follow me and I will guide you to the Straight Path.
ayahs.44: O dear father, do not worship Satan. Satan is ever rebellious against the Rahman.
ayahs.45: O dear father, I fear a torment from the Rahman will touch you, and you will become Satan's companion."
ayahs.46: He threatened: "How dare you reject my idols, O Abraham? If you do not stop, I will stone you. Leave me for a long time!"
ayahs.47: Abraham replied: "Peace be upon you. I will ask my Rabb to forgive you. He has been gracious to me.
ayahs.48: As I leave you and what you invoke besides Allah, I will call upon my Rabb alone, trusting I will never be disappointed in calling upon Him."
ayahs.49: After he left them and what they worshipped besides Allah, We granted him Isaac and Jacob, making each a prophet.
ayahs.50: We showered them with Our mercy and blessed them with honourable mention.
ayahs.51: And mention Moses in the Book. He was truly chosen—a messenger and prophet.
ayahs.52: We called him from the right side of Mount Tur and drew him near for direct conversation.
ayahs.53: Out of Our grace We appointed his brother Aaron as a prophet.
ayahs.54: And mention Ishmael in the Book. He was true to his word—a messenger and prophet.
ayahs.55: He used to urge his people to establish salah and give zakat. His Rabb was well pleased with him.
ayahs.56: And mention Enoch in the Book. He was a man of truth and a prophet.
ayahs.57: We elevated him to an honourable station.
ayahs.58: Those were among the prophets Allah blessed—from Adam's descendants, from those carried with Noah, from Abraham and Israel's line, and from those We guided and chose. When the revelations of the Rahman were recited to them, they fell prostrating, weeping.
ayahs.59: But later generations neglected salah and followed their nafs—the inner self that pulls toward desire—so they will soon face evil consequences.
ayahs.60: Those who repent, believe, and do good will enter Paradise, never denied their reward.
ayahs.61: Gardens of Eternity, promised in trust by the Rahman to His servants. His promise will be fulfilled.
ayahs.62: There they will hear no idle talk—only peace. Their provision will be morning and evening.
ayahs.63: That is Paradise, which We grant to whoever among Our servants lives with taqwa.
ayahs.64: We only descend by your Rabb's command. To Him belongs what is before us, behind us, and everything between. Your Rabb is never forgetful.
ayahs.65: Lord of the heavens, earth, and all between. So worship Him alone and persevere in His worship. Do you know anyone equal to Him?
ayahs.66: Yet people ask mockingly: "After I die, will I really be raised to life?"
ayahs.67: Do they not remember We created them before when they were nothing?
ayahs.68: By your Rabb, We will gather them with the devils, then set them around Hell on their knees.
ayahs.69: We will begin by dragging from every group those most defiant toward the Rahman.
ayahs.70: We know best who is most deserving of burning in it.
ayahs.71: None of you will fail to pass over it. This is a decree your Rabb must fulfil.
ayahs.72: Then We will deliver those who lived with taqwa, leaving wrongdoers kneeling in it.
ayahs.73: When Our clear revelations are recited, those who reject the truth ask the believers mockingly: "Which of us is better in status and superior in assembly?"
ayahs.74: How many peoples We destroyed before them who were far better in luxury and splendour!
ayahs.75: Say: "Whoever is entrenched in misguidance, the Rahman will allow them plenty of time—until they face what they were warned of: torment or the Hour. Then they will know who is worse in position and weaker in support."
ayahs.76: Allah increases guidance for those already guided. Everlasting good deeds are far better with your Rabb in reward and outcome.
ayahs.77: Have you seen one who rejects Our revelations yet boasts: "I will definitely be granted wealth and children"?
ayahs.78: Has he looked into the unseen or taken a pledge from the Rahman?
ayahs.79: No. We record what he claims and will extend his punishment extensively.
ayahs.80: We will inherit what he boasts of, and he will come before Us alone.
ayahs.81: They have taken gods besides Allah, seeking strength through them.
ayahs.82: But those gods will deny their worship and turn against them.
ayahs.83: Do you not see We have sent devils against those who reject the truth, constantly inciting them?
ayahs.84: Do not be in haste against them. We are closely counting down their days.
ayahs.85: Watch for the Day We gather the righteous before the Rahman as an honoured delegation,
ayahs.86: and drive the wicked to Hell like a thirsty herd.
ayahs.87: None will intercede except those granted permission by the Rahman.
ayahs.88: They say: "The Rahman has taken offspring."
ayahs.89: You have made an outrageous claim—
ayahs.90: by which the heavens nearly burst, the earth splits, and mountains crumble
ayahs.91: in protest at attributing children to the Rahman.
ayahs.92: It does not befit the Rahman to have children.
ayahs.93: Everyone in the heavens and earth will return to the Rahman in full submission.
ayahs.94: He fully knows them and has counted them precisely.
ayahs.95: Each will return to Him on the Day of Judgment alone.
ayahs.96: Those who believe and do good—the Rahman will bless them with genuine love.
ayahs.97: We made this Quran easy in your language so you may give good news to those with taqwa and warn those who are contentious.
ayahs.98: How many generations We destroyed before them! Do you see any of them, or hear even a whisper from them?
